blocks.1: The stone baptismal font in Gulen church. For baptisms today a silver bowl is placed in the stone.
blocks.2: Everyone has probably heard the legend of how the baptismal font came to be. In the booklet from the Gulating gathering of 10 July 1938 it is told like this: “Many of the common people whom King Olav forced to be baptised at the Gulating were very unwilling. And the people of Sogn were especially ‘stubborn’. It is told that they even kicked the font out of the hands of the court bishop Grimkjell. Then Olav had a font made of stone. The sturdy men of Sogn would find it hard to overturn that.”
blocks.3: The font is shaped like a large cube, about 60 cm square, with a hollow carved out to hold the baptismal water. Such a “block of stone” they surely could not kick away. It appears to be made of the same kind of stone as the two stone crosses. It used to stand next to the Olav cross by the churchyard gate.
blocks.4: According to a tradition recorded by Absalon Taranger (1893) from a Bertel Gjeitnæs, a priest, probably Dressing, moved the stone down to Borggarden, but Dahl moved it back up to the cross. Dahl is said to have said: “That is where it belongs; we must preserve this old memorial.” It is said that while the font stood down by the sea, the priest used it to keep fish in water. I have also heard that it was built into a wall. A third version is that it was found in the steps of the cookhouse at the parsonage (Birkeli p. 179).
blocks.5: Information that Olav Midthun (farm no. 15, holding no. 34) had from “Niklas i Garden” suggests that in earlier times a small church stood down by the sea, where the road now runs westwards north of “Herresalen”. Visible traces of the church site are also said to have been there. Niklas (Nikolai) was a tenant at the parsonage right up to about 1910. The house he lived in stood up against the stone wall, roughly where the wall turns east from Krossteigen. Since I have this from only one source, we cannot really call it a tradition, but Niklas hardly told this without some basis, and if a church did stand there, that may be the right explanation of why the font was found down here by the sea.
blocks.6: Westerlund said that the font stood inside the first church built here, a small, simple wooden church, but when the church was destroyed the font ended up outside and did not come back into the church until a very long time afterwards.
blocks.7: In his book Bjordø believes that the font was placed in the present church in 1905. The local historian Karl Gåta said the same. Alf Sæternes says, from what his parents Ingeborg and Anders Sæternes told him, that they remembered the font coming into the church then, because they married that year. It was a stand-in priest who was here, Gundersen, who arranged for the stone to be placed inside the church, where it still stands and is in use as a font.
blocks.8: In “Fremad”, the handwritten paper of the Eivindvik youth society, for 29 December 1905, I have also found something about this. It says of the stand-in priest Gundersen, among other things: “Before he left he did a fine deed together with the church council. You have all seen the square stone next to the Olav cross outside the churchyard gate. The old baptismal font that has stood there exposed to lye and cold water, neglected for many years. Now Gunnarson and the others got it back into its proper place in the church. Not that – for anyone who thought about it – it was not in a way an honourable place it had next to the Olav cross too.”
